ox_lexicographer.text: The Oxford English Dictionary! We trace every word back to its first use, with quotations. 'Dodo' is in there, with a note that nobody is sure whether it comes from a Portuguese word for a fool or a Dutch one.

It took seventy years to finish the first edition, from 1857 to 1928. The editor, James Murray, sorted the paper slips in a corrugated iron shed in his garden in north Oxford, called the Scriptorium. His children helped.

ox_wordsmith.text: Volunteers sent in millions of slips. One of the busiest was an American army surgeon, W. C. Minor, who sent thousands from the secure hospital where he lived. Murray thought he was a colleague for years, and then went to visit.
The Dictionary is online now and updated every quarter. It has more than 600,000 words and never once says no. It just says: 'earliest known use'.
